t: The Bahá’í Faith grew from the movement of the Báb, a merchant of Shiraz who in 1844 proclaimed a new revelation, and from the mission of Bahá’u’lláh, who in 1863 declared himself the messenger of God whom the Báb had foretold.

It teaches that the founders of the great religions were messengers of one God, and that humanity must unite in a peaceful world order, with the equality of women and men, universal education and the harmony of science and religion.
Persecuted in Iran from its beginnings to the present day, it spread from its founders’ places of exile in the Ottoman Empire to almost every country, with its world centre in Haifa and Acre.
dyk: The Bahá’í calendar has nineteen months of nineteen days; during the last month, in March, Bahá’ís fast from sunrise to sunset before celebrating their New Year, Naw-Rúz, at the spring equinox.
ev: The Báb declares his mission in Shiraz
The Báb is executed by a firing squad in Tabriz
Bahá’u’lláh declares his mission in the Garden of Ridván in Baghdad
Bahá’u’lláh is exiled to the Ottoman prison city of Acre
Bahá’u’lláh dies near Acre; his son ʻAbdu’l-Bahá leads the faith
ʻAbdu’l-Bahá travels across North America, speaking in churches, synagogues and universities
The Universal House of Justice, the faith’s governing body, is elected for the first time
More than two hundred Bahá’ís are executed or killed in Iran in the years after the Islamic Revolution

f.origin: Qajar Iran: the Báb’s declaration in Shiraz in 1844 and Bahá’u’lláh’s declaration in Baghdad in 1863
f.scriptures: The writings of Bahá’u’lláh, among them the Kitáb-i-Aqdas and the Kitáb-i-Íqán, with those of the Báb and the interpretations of ʻAbdu’l-Bahá
f.followers: Estimates range from about five to eight million, in almost every country of the world
